sections.h2: Where is Brookings and what is it known for?
sections.html:
Brookings is the county seat of Brookings County, about 60 miles north of Sioux Falls along Interstate 29, and it is best known as the home of South Dakota State University. The city covers roughly 14 square miles at an elevation of 1,660 feet.

The railroad's first train reached Main Street on October 18, 1879, and the city was incorporated on March 9, 1883. It was named for pioneer promoter Wilmot Brookings. The 2020 census counted 23,377 residents, which made it the fourth most populous city in the state.

  • County seat of Brookings County
  • Interstate 29 Exit 132 is the only exit signed for Brookings
  • U.S. Highway 14 also runs through the area

sections.h2: How much does the university shape the Brookings housing market?
sections.html:
South Dakota State University is the state's largest institution of higher education, with 12,065 students enrolled in fall 2024. The school is also the city's largest employer, which gives Brookings a rhythm tied to the academic calendar.

That rhythm shows up in the housing stock. Duplexes, older single-family homes near campus and student rentals sit alongside family neighborhoods on the edge of town. Owners who inherited a rental or who rented to students for years often find themselves selling a house with worn finishes and a tenant lease that runs to a fixed date. Timing a sale around the spring and summer lease cycle can matter more here than in a city without a large campus.

sections.html:

A tight local job market tends to keep demand for homes steady, though it does not guarantee a quick or high-priced sale for a house that needs work.

sections.h2: What does a Brookings winter do to a house?
sections.html:
Brookings has a humid continental climate with long, cold winters, and the numbers explain why heating costs and frozen pipes come up so often. Mean daily temperature runs from 12.8 degrees in January to 70.7 degrees in July.

  • About 35 days a year with lows below zero
  • About 8 days a year at 90 degrees or higher
  • Snowfall of about 35.8 inches a year
  • Precipitation of about 25.21 inches a year, mostly in the warmer months

Cold snaps put stress on furnaces, water heaters and older plumbing. Spring melt tests sump pumps and basement walls. Buyers' inspectors in Brookings routinely look at the furnace age, window condition and signs of water in the lower level. A seller who knows the answers before the inspection is better placed to negotiate.

sections.h2: Is flood risk a factor for Brookings sellers?
sections.html:
It can be for houses near creeks. The city's Engineering Division maintains pages on floodplains and on Six-Mile Creek flood risk mitigation, and the city's future land use map overlays the Six Mile Creek and Deer Creek floodplains.

FEMA publishes the floodplain delineation, so the first step for an owner is to look up the parcel on FEMA's map or ask the city's engineering staff. Lenders require flood insurance on a mortgaged house inside a mapped Special Flood Hazard Area, and a buyer will ask about it. The seller's disclosure form also asks about flood plains, so the answer has to be written down either way.

sections.h2: What are the rules for rental houses in Brookings?
sections.html:
Brookings inspects and licenses rental dwellings through its Code Enforcement office. Rental properties are inspected and licensed for up to four years, or as an ordinance requires, and each unit is licensed for a maximum number of occupants.

  • The licensing form is the Rental Housing Permit Application.
  • Tenants with occupancy concerns can use the city's complaint form.
  • The city page does not list fees; Code Enforcement can be reached at (605) 692-6629.

A landlord selling a licensed rental should find out when the license expires and what occupant limit applies, because a buyer who plans to keep the tenants will ask. A lapsed license or an old inspection finding is easier to fix before the sale than after a contract is signed.

sections.h2: How and when are Brookings County property taxes paid?
sections.html:
Brookings County collects the first half of the year's property tax by April 30 and the second half by October 31. Taxes can be paid in full once notices go out in January. All special assessments, and any tax bill under $50, are due in full by April 30.

  • Pay in person at 520 3rd Street, Suite 100, Brookings, SD 57006, by mail, online or through the drop box on the west side of the building.
  • Credit cards carry a 2.5 percent service fee at the counter.
  • Mailed payments must be postmarked on or before the due date.
  • Partial payments are not accepted for taxes that are due or delinquent.

The county's Auditor and Treasurer functions share one office. Relief programs listed there include the Disabled Veteran and Surviving Spouse exemption and the Senior Citizens and Disabled assessment freeze. On a sale, the unpaid share of the current bill is normally settled through the title company at closing.

sections.h2: What paperwork does a Brookings sale need?
sections.html:
South Dakota law requires a property condition disclosure from the seller, and the deed needs a Certificate of Real Estate Value (PT 56) before the register of deeds will record it. The state form, dated 07/2025, asks about liens, easements, drainage, the roof, radon, lead paint, mold and the working status of about 47 systems and appliances.

The transfer fee comes from SDCL 43-4-21, and SDCL 43-4-22 lists 19 exemptions. Minnehaha County's schedule shows $1.00 per thousand, and the Brookings County Register of Deeds can confirm its own recording fee and the amount due on your sale.

sections.h2: Which schools and travel options serve Brookings?
sections.html:
Brookings School District 05-1 covers almost all of the city and serves pre-K through grade 12. It enrolled 3,446 students in 2022-23, and its schools include Brookings High School, George S. Mickelson Middle School and Camelot Intermediate. A small part of the city lies in Sioux Valley School District 05-5.

Brookings Regional Airport had a major reconstruction in 2012, and Jefferson Lines offers intercity bus service. Sioux Falls is about 60 miles south on Interstate 29.

sections.h2: When does a cash sale make sense in Brookings?
sections.html:
A cash sale suits a Brookings owner who needs speed or does not want to repair and show a house. Inherited homes, worn student rentals and houses with deferred maintenance are the usual cases.

We buy Brookings houses as-is, with no repairs required, and you owe nothing if you decline the offer.

faqs.q: How many people live in Brookings, SD?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 25,355 residents as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 census counted 23,377.

faqs.q: Do Brookings rental houses need a license?
faqs.a: Yes. The city's Code Enforcement office inspects and licenses rental dwellings for up to four years, with a maximum occupant count for each unit.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Brookings County?
faqs.a: The first half is due April 30 and the second half October 31. Special assessments and any tax under $50 are due in full by April 30.

faqs.q: Can I pay Brookings County taxes online?
faqs.a: Yes. The county accepts online payments by card, PayPal or e-check, in addition to in-person, mail and drop-box payments. Card payments at the counter carry a 2.5 percent service fee.

faqs.q: Does a Brookings seller have to complete a disclosure form?
faqs.a: Yes. South Dakota requires the seller's property condition disclosure statement to be given to the buyer.

faqs.q: What is the Certificate of Real Estate Value?
faqs.a: The PT 56 lists the buyer, seller, legal description, price and payment terms. The register of deeds cannot accept a deed without it.
